item.title: KIMBLE A CANDIDATE FOR USD 367 SUPER
item.description: USD 367, Osawatomie, will have a new superintendent next school year. One of the final candidates is Scott Kimble. Scott is the principal at Osawatomie High School and has 27 years experience in public education, including 13 years in building leadership. item.title: GARNETT SUBSTANCE IDENTIFIED
item.description: Last week, the EPA released it’s finding on the mysterious substance that was spilled on a Garnett Roadway on New Year’s eve. The material was identified as sodium aluminate. Sodium aluminate is a chemical compound that is typically used in water and wastewater treatment, paper and glass manufacturing, and as a solidification accelerant in the construction industry. item.title: COF GETS BIG GRANT
item.description: COF Training Services, has secured a $500,000 Capstone Challenge Grant from the J. E. & L. E. Mabee Foundation of Tulsa, Ok, for its capital campaign. CEO Patrick Gardner says the campaign was their first multimillion dollar drive in their 58 year history. He says the campaign has raised more than $3 million for capital projects that enhance workforce development for COF individuals. item.title: FIRE SCHOOL
item.description: K-State Research and Extension, Frontier District, in partnership with the Anderson County Conservation District, will host a prescribed burn school designed to help landowners and producers plan and safely carry out effective burns. item.title: MORAN ON ROTOR ACT
item.description: Just over a year has passed since a tragic crash at Reagan Airport in Washington D. C. claimed the lives of 67 people in an airplane that struck a military helicopter.
